title: Per-route availability contract and priority-driven degradation playbook
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: Produce a prescriptive contract that defines per-route KPIs (availability, latency, and quality), a deterministic error-budget allocation model across regions and model variants, and an operational playbook for priority-driven graceful degradation (circuit breakers and load-shedding) for model endpoints.

Scope: This ticket covers user-visible LLM routes (chat, completion, embeddings, reranking). For each route we will: 1) define SLIs and measurement windows, 2) allocate error budget shares to model variants and regions, 3) specify circuit-breaker thresholds and hysteresis, and 4) provide a step-by-step failover & load-shedding matrix by customer priority class. It explicitly excludes low-level kernel scheduling optimizations and billing/quotas integration (handled by ENG-76230).

Definitions and proposed SLIs: 
- Availability SLI: fraction of successful responses (HTTP 2xx + domain-quality pass) within 30s per rolling 1h window.
- Latency SLI: p95 server-side generation latency measured at token-completion for served responses excluding streaming handshakes.
- Quality SLI: route-specific QA pass-rate evaluated on a representative prompt set (daily rolling 24h sample); quality SLI is considered 'violated' if pass-rate drops by >3 percentage points vs baseline.

Error budget allocation model (high level): 
- Each route has a 99.9% availability SLO (configurable by customer tier). Error budget is expressed in minutes per 30-day window.
- Budget partitioning: 60% pooled to regional availability, 30% assigned to model-variant degradations (e.g., quantized variants), 10% reserved as emergency credit for cross-region evacuation.
- 'Degradation credits': when a model-variant consumes budget, downstream routing can progressively route to cheaper/quantized fallback variants until budget exhaustion triggers circuit-breakers.

Priority classes and behavioral guarantees: 
- P1 (critical): retained for enterprise paid SLAs. Degradation allowed only to compatible model-variants within same quality band; cross-region failover prioritized before model degradation.
- P2 (standard): prefer local region; allow model-variant fallback aggressively before cross-region failover.
- P3 (best-effort/free): aggressive load-shedding at the route gateway, fallbacks to zero-cost skeleton responses allowed.

Circuit breaker & load-shedding rules: 
- Two-tier circuit breakers per route: latency-circuit (triggered by p95 > threshold) and error-circuit (triggered by API error rate increase).
- Thresholds are route-specific (example: chat latency threshold p95=600ms for P1). Triggers: 3 consecutive 5-minute windows above threshold.
- Hysteresis: soft-open period 5m with partial throttling, hard-open 15m with progressive shedding by priority class.
- Load-shedding matrix: 1) request-level throttling by priority token quota, 2) degrade to quantized variant, 3) fall back to summary/latent cache, 4) return graceful degradation response with retry-after header.

Multi-region evacuation & failover: 
- Evacuation triggers: complete region loss (control plane signals), or region-level sustained error budget breach >80% of allocated window.
- Failover order for P1: local region -> nearest region with reserved emergency credit -> global fallback cluster.
- Metadata & routing: propagation via Control Plane feature flag; all requests during failover must carry provenance headers for postmortem attribution.

Monitoring, dashboards & runbooks: 
- Dashboards required: per-route availability heatmap, per-model-variant error-budget burn rate, regional evacuation status, and circuit-breaker state streams.
- Alerting: burn-rate alerts at 25/50/80% and automatic runbook links on first alert.
- Runbooks: step-by-step for engineers to manually apply traffic caps, kick off model rollbacks, and request capacity reservations.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Canonical SLI definitions documented and published in Confluence.
2) Error-budget calculator implemented in the Console (simulated for any window).
3) Circuit-breaker prototype wired into one pilot route (chat-prod) with dashboards and synthetic tests.
4) Playbook and runbooks reviewed by oncall, SRE, and PM and marked approved.

Open questions and trade-offs: 
- How to reconcile quality SLI detection latency vs real user impact (we sample daily; could be slow for fast regressions). Proposal: add a small set of high-frequency 'sentinel' prompts for faster detection.
- Granularity of budget partitioning between model variants vs regions; current split is opinionated and may adjust after the pilot.
- Interaction with existing per-customer quotas and billing: we will coordinate with billing team in follow-up ticket.

Risks: Wrongly tuned thresholds may cause premature degradation and poor customer experience. Overly conservative failover increases cross-region egress and cost.

Next steps: implement prototypes for chat-prod, run chaos tests (simulated region loss), and gather burn-rate telemetry for one month before wider rollout.
comments: 2026-02-20 Marco Chen: Initial RFC created with proposed SLIs and error-budget partitioning. Asked SRE to review thresholds and workload sampling plan.

2026-02-26 Priya Patel (SRE): Reviewed. Suggested adding a sentinel prompt set for quality SLI and lowering p95 threshold for embeddings routes. Action: SRE to provide recommended thresholds by 2026-03-05.
2026-03-01 Design review (Rafael Gomez): Approved playbook UX for Console error-budget visualization; requested example user-facing degradation messages and retry semantics.
2026-03-05 Aisha Bhattacharya: Implemented initial circuit-breaker prototype on chat-prod branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423. Tests included for soft-open behavior.

2026-03-08 Marco Chen: Ran chaos experiment (simulated region egress outage). Observations: model-variant fallback reduced burn rate but introduced a 1.5% quality drop for P2. Logged follow-up to tune fallback ordering.
2026-03-10 PM feedback (Leah Kim): Request to surface per-customer error budget usage in Billing Console for enterprise customers; created cross-team ticket ENG-77244.
2026-03-10 Aisha Bhattacharya: Draft runbook uploaded to Confluence and linked below. Ready for SRE dry-run on 2026-03-18.
